headline: Jerónimo had a fall on 9/25 and new evening confusion since about mid-October, including a stove left on. His caregiver, his grandson Robert, reported exhaustion on 11/22 and asked for respite.

items.statement: On 11/2 Robert reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, with the stove left on once. Jerónimo was oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The nurse planned a urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit that week. No results or PCP visit for this concern appear in the notes provided.
items.verifier_note: All details match the 11/2 note. The 'no results or PCP visit in notes' statement is an accurate absence claim, since only this note is cited.

items.statement: On 9/25 Jerónimo fell at home getting out of bed and was found on the floor by his grandson. He denied head strike and loss of consciousness. He had a small left forearm skin tear, which was cleaned and dressed. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed.
items.verifier_note: The 9/25 note matches every detail: the fall getting out of bed, the grandson finding him, no head strike or LOC, the left forearm skin tear cleaned and dressed, high fall risk, and the PT referral.

items.statement: On 11/22 Robert, the primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.
items.verifier_note: Matches the 11/22 social work note: exhaustion, poor sleep, worry about evenings alone, respite request, and discussion of respite options and a support group.

items.statement: The PT evaluation on 9/29 found gait slow and unsteady with intermittent cane use, and Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, and planned twice-weekly strength and balance sessions. The notes provided do not show whether the walker, home evaluation or grab bars are in place.
items.verifier_note: The PT evaluation note matches all details: slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use, TUG 19 seconds, the walker, home safety evaluation and grab bar recommendations, and twice-weekly sessions. The note says nothing about whether the equipment is in place, so the absence statement is accurate.

items.statement: No flu vaccine is recorded for the current season, which began 8/1/2026. The most recent flu vaccine was 6/30/2026, before the season start.
items.verifier_note: The immunization record shows flu_vaccine_this_season false, a season start of 8/1/2026, and a most recent flu vaccine on 6/30/2026, which is before the season start.

questions_for_team: Were the urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit ordered on 11/2 completed, and what were the results? The 11/13 nursing note says 'no new concerns' and does not mention the confusion.
What interim evening supervision and stove safety measures can be put in place while the confusion is evaluated?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in it: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, observation stays, and any readmissions, given the new ischemic heart disease diagnosis dated 2026-06-30.

Cardiac events and symptoms: chest pain or angina episodes, nitroglycerin spray use and frequency, dyspnea, syncope, palpitations, and any ECG, troponin, stress test, or cardiology referral or follow-up since onset of ischemic heart disease.

Cardiac medication review: confirm metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, simvastatin, and nitroglycerin spray were started as listed (2026-07-07) and are being taken as prescribed; check for missed doses, refill gaps, and any dose changes, holds, or discontinuations in the window.

Bleeding and antiplatelet safety: on clopidogrel with a history of dependent drug abuse and chronic pain. Check for bleeding, bruising, GI symptoms, melena, hematuria, and any NSAID or OTC analgesic use reported or dispensed; check labs (CBC) if drawn.

Blood pressure and heart rate trend across the window, including orthostatic readings if recorded, given beta-blocker and nitrate therapy; flag dizziness, falls, or fatigue reported alongside readings.

Falls and fracture risk: any falls, near-falls, or injuries in the window, given osteoporosis, scoliosis, and a new cardiac and antiplatelet regimen. Confirm alendronic acid adherence (take-with-water, upright 30 minutes) and check for dental or jaw concerns, since impacted molars are on the problem list.

Bone health follow-up: check whether a DXA result, calcium/vitamin D status, or a bone health plan is documented and due; note the alendronate start date of 2026-06-30 and any renal function or dental review noted.

Pain and migraine review: current pain scores, opioid or other controlled-substance prescriptions and dispensing history, migraine frequency and acute treatments used, and any new analgesics. Look for interactions or overlap with the cardiac regimen and for early refill patterns.

Substance use and recovery: review documented status for dependent drug abuse (use, relapse, treatment engagement, naloxone availability, prescriber or pharmacy flags), and any changes in support services or attendance at recovery programs.

Function, cognition, mood, weight, and caregiver: check ADL/IADL changes, cognitive screen results, depression or anxiety screens given the new cardiac diagnosis, BMI and weight trend (obesity on problem list), social supports and caregiver availability, and any care-plan items or assessments that are due or overdue in the window.
